div.div: Root cause starts where the sequence leaves the normal path: partition the log by thread, count transitions, and compare them with the golden sequence mined from many devices
A. One interleaved stream, two threads [A1, B5] (toy lines)
same timestamp on two lines (ms resolution): true order unknown

thread 845, sorted by time
scan start -> assoc start -> auth ok -> connected -> disconnected -> network bounce

trap: sort the whole log by time
scan start -> dhcp renew -> assoc start -> dhcp ack ... gives edges that never happen in the code. Partition by pid/tid first.

Transition count matrix A (N x N templates) [B5]: for each consecutive pair (i, j) inside one thread, A[i][j] += 1. Skip the edge into a task-start template so one task's end is not linked to the next. Drop impossible timestamps (cache replayed after a reboot). Ties average out over many windows.
B. Workflow (empirical control-flow graph) from many healthy devices [B5]
golden sequence (green): the normal order for the task, shown next to the anomalous one
sequence anomaly: an expected child does not appear within its usual lag after its parent (missing in thread 845)
distribution anomaly: the probability of an edge changes. After 'disconnected' the share to 'reconnect success' (thick) falls, the share to 'network bounce' rises.

The graph is the OBSERVED graph, not the code's: paths the code allows but healthy devices never take are absent, so their appearance is itself a signal. Normal transition statistics need many devices over long periods.

1 Narrow the search (cascade) [B5]: the metric says which devices, roughly when, and what (e.g. disconnects with reason 15). Traps: metrics aggregated hourly or daily; device logs in local time, metrics in UTC.

2 Show the departure [B5]: golden sequence beside the anomalous one; state-machine search (ordered events + max time span -> every match with raw lines); a chosen parameter over time; replay through the print statements if templates map to code.

3 Hypothesis, not verdict [B5, C4]: the anomalous template is often a symptom downstream of the cause in another component (DHCP, time sync, a kernel driver). Output = top windows, top templates, the departing edge, the raw lines.

Legend — blue / purple = lines of two threads; green = normal workflow and golden sequence (edge thickness = share of transitions); red dashed = anomaly (missing child, shifted edge, wrong sort); amber = the triggering event and the human step. Toy lines, no data.

Sources — every number is loaded from ../constants.json. [n] = public (real value, cited); [n*] = illustrative (an invented round number of realistic order of magnitude; never a measurement). Workflow idea: Du et al., DeepLog, CCS 2017, §4.4.
[1] ieee80211_reason_4way_handshake_timeout = 15 reason code — public; IEEE Std 802.11 reason-code table; wpa_supplicant ieee802_11_defs.h (WLAN_REASON_4WAY_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT)
